transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: When I first started here, a couple months later, I met my girlfriend. I brought her to a date here after hours. That might not technically be allowed.
transcript.zh: 我刚来这儿干了没几个月，就认识了我女朋友。我带她打烊后来这儿约会。严格来说，这可能不太合规定。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: What do you mean, after hours?
transcript.zh: 什么叫“打烊后”？

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: Oh, everything was closed. We were closed down. I asked her if she wanted to come see a movie, so we watched Wicked.
transcript.zh: 哦，就是影院都关门了，已经停止营业了。我问她想不想来看场电影，于是我们就看了《魔法坏女巫》。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: Whoa, you brought your girlfriend here because you had the keys to the place.
transcript.zh: 哇，你是凭着手里有影院钥匙，直接把女朋友带进来的啊。

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: I did. I had the keys. She wasn't actually my girlfriend quite yet. Good first date.
transcript.zh: 对，我有钥匙。不过那会儿她还算不上我女朋友呢。很棒的第一次约会。

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: I knew Wicked was one of her favorite musicals. So it was like, perfect thing. Wicked just came out. Why don't we watch it? Private showing in the biggest screen we can.
transcript.zh: 我知道《魔法坏女巫》是她最喜欢的音乐剧之一，所以简直天赐良机。电影刚上映，不如一起来看？用最大号银幕来一场私人专场。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: Darren ushered her into an empty theater, sat her down in the best seat in the house. Popcorn, Diet Coke in the cup holder. Brought a sweater because theaters get chilly.
transcript.zh: Darren 把她领进空无一人的放映厅，请她坐在全场最佳座位上。杯托里插着健怡可乐，还备好了爆米花，甚至带了件毛衣——因为影厅里冷气很足。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: And then he ran up to the projectionist booth, fast forwarded through the ads, and ran back down to sit with her just in time for the show to start.
transcript.zh: 接着他一路跑上放映室，快进跳过所有贴片广告，又跑回厅里，卡在正片开场前刚好坐到她身边。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: That was two years ago. Now they're engaged. What other job would let you pull off a first date like that?
transcript.zh: 那是两年前的事了，如今他俩已经订婚了。还有哪份工作能让你整出这么浪漫的初次约会？

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: Honestly, I mean, it was so memorable. We still think about it.
transcript.zh: 说实话，那次真的太难忘了。我们到现在还经常回味。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: Now, tell me if I'm overstating it, but would you guys be getting married if it wasn't for that?
transcript.zh: 这么说可能有点夸张，但你告诉我，要不是那场约会，你们俩现在能走到结婚这一步吗？

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: I would hope so, but I don't know. It's a good question because of how big of a thing it was and how meaningful and unique it was that it definitely bumped me up some points.
transcript.zh: 我当然希望如此，但真说不准。这个问题问得好，因为那晚真的意义非凡又独一无二，绝对给我加了不少分。

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: So hopefully, but definitely not as easily.
transcript.zh: 所以但愿也会成吧，但肯定没这么顺理成章。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: It's really similar to the thing that happened to me.
transcript.zh: 这跟我当年遇到的事简直如出一辙。

transcript.speaker: Darren Klingaman
transcript.en: Okay.
transcript.zh: 哦？

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: When I was here-- I told Darren that I also once tried to impress a girl while on the job. When I met her, I filled up a discarded plastic bag with popcorn and slipped it to her. Another time, I let her and her friend in the back.
transcript.zh: 我在这儿干的时候——我跟 Darren 讲，我当年上班时也试过讨好一个女孩。刚认识她那会儿，我用个废弃塑料袋装满爆米花偷偷塞给她。还有一次，我从后门把她和她朋友放了进来。

transcript.speaker: Ike Sriskandarajah
transcript.en: I'm no longer wearing a tuxedo to work, but that girl I snuck in, we're married and have two children. The job today definitely seems less fun, but there's still a little movie magic left.
transcript.zh: 如今我上班早就不用穿无尾礼服了，但当年那个被我偷偷放进来的女孩，现在已经成了我太太，我们还有了两个孩子。现在的影院工作确实没以前那么好玩了，但大银幕的魔法，多少还留了一点。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Ike Sriskandarajah. He's one of the producers of our show. By the way, none of the three teenagers I talked to knew what chode meant, but some of them thought it was funny anyway.
transcript.zh: 以上就是 Ike Sriskandarajah 带来的报道，他是我们节目的制作人之一。顺便一提，我问过的那三个青少年里，没一个知道 chode 是什么意思，但有几个还是觉得挺好笑的。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Act Three: Mama, Can You Hair Me? Myra Flynn is in her 40s, and the person across the divide in this story is six. It's her daughter.
transcript.zh: Act Three：Mama, Can You Hair Me?。Myra Flynn 四十多岁了，而这个故事里和她站在“代沟”另一头的人只有六岁——是她的女儿。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: The two of them have been in a bit of a standoff when it comes to getting ready for school in the morning. It was going so badly, Myra started recording these morning showdowns, trying to figure out if there was some way to fix things. Here she is.
transcript.zh: 每天早上准备去上学时，母女俩都会陷入一场僵持。情况糟到 Myra 开始把这些清晨“对峙”录下来，想看看有没有什么办法能化解。下面来听她的故事。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: My mornings used to look so different. In my younger days as a touring musician, I'd greet the sunrise on my way home from a gig in some random city and face plant into my bed.
transcript.zh: 我以前的早晨完全不是这样的。年轻时我是一名巡演音乐人，经常在某个不知名的城市演出完，迎着日出回家，然后一头栽倒在床上。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: But now, I start my day at 7:10 AM, engaged in a battle of wills with my daughter Avalon over her hair.
transcript.zh: 可现在，我每天早上七点十分准时开启新的一天——为了给女儿 Avalon 梳头，跟她展开一场意志力的拉锯战。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Hey, baby. It's time to do your hair. No, we're going to do it because you got to be at school in 10 minutes.
transcript.zh: 嘿，宝贝，该梳头了。不行，必须得梳，你十分钟后就得赶到学校了。

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: But Mommy.
transcript.zh: 可是妈妈……

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: When I was a kid, my mom and I had a similar hair routine. She would sit me down at the breakfast table every morning, grab a cup of water and a hard bristle brush, and rake through my curls.
transcript.zh: 我小时候，我妈和我也天天上演差不多的梳头戏码。每天早上她都会按着我坐在餐桌前，抓起一杯水和一把硬毛刷，狠狠地梳过我的卷发。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: It hurt like hell, but there was no point in complaining because my mom made it clear we didn't have time for any of that. My hair had to get done.
transcript.zh: 那叫一个疼啊，但抱怨也没用，因为我妈把话挑得很明白：我们可没时间搞这些有的没的，这头发必须得梳。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: That's just how it was. And that's just how it is for Avalon. Black hair is Black hair.
transcript.zh: 以前就是这么过来的，现在 Avalon 也逃不掉。黑人的头发就是这样。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And look, I'm not doing box braids or knotless styles, or writing her name in the side of her head with cornrows. I'm just trying to comb through it and put it in a ponytail so that no one looks at us crazy.
transcript.zh: 你别误会，我又不是要给她编盒式脏辫、无结辫，或者用玉米辫在她脑袋侧面编出她的名字。我只是想把头发梳通，扎个马尾，好让别人别用看疯子一样的眼神盯着我们。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: So every morning, I take her hair out of whatever shape it's landed in after a night of sleep without a bonnet. I still haven't found one that stays on her head.
transcript.zh: 所以每天早上，我都得把她没戴护发睡帽折腾了一宿、压成各种奇形怪状的头发理顺。我到现在还没找到一顶能老老实实待在她头上的睡帽。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Then I grab three different brushes, a big jar of leave-in conditioner, a spray bottle full of water, and get to work, which Avalon, who's six, hates.
transcript.zh: 接着我抄起三把不同的梳子、一大罐免洗护发素、一瓶装满水的喷雾，正式开工——而六岁的 Avalon 对此深恶痛绝。

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Ow!
transcript.zh: 哎哟！

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Stop, baby. Avi, it's not that bad. Stop, stop, stop.
transcript.zh: 别动了，宝贝。Avi，真没那么疼。停下，停下，停下。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: No, no. I can't use that brush. I have to use this brush.
transcript.zh: 不行，不行，我不能用那把梳子，我必须得用这把。

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: I just wanted to hold it.
transcript.zh: 我只是想拿着它嘛。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: No, baby. You need to just-- please, can you just look forward, and bend your neck for me. Bend your neck down.
transcript.zh: 不行，宝贝，你得……求你了，能就看着前面吗，把脖子低下来，低下来一点。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: For the record, holding this brush is a stalling tactic for Avalon. She wants to hold it so I can't use it.
transcript.zh: 我得说明一下，要拿着这把梳子是 Avalon 的拖延战术。她把它攥在手里，我就没法用了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And I see straight through you, Avalon Mathis Wills. I know my daughter.
transcript.zh: Avalon Mathis Wills，你这点小心思我一眼就看穿了。我太了解我女儿了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Avalon, by all intents and purposes, seems impervious to pain. I've literally watched her face plant from the top of monkey bars onto the grass, only to bounce up and try it again.
transcript.zh: 不管从哪方面看，Avalon 简直是个“痛觉绝缘体”。我亲眼见过她从攀爬架顶上直接脸朝下摔进草地里，结果一骨碌爬起来接着再试一次。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: This is a kid who doesn't want to wait for her teeth to fall out naturally. As soon as they're loose, she's trying to pull them out of her head.
transcript.zh: 这孩子连乳牙自然脱落都等不及，只要一松动，她就想亲手把牙从嘴里拔下来。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And she won't even let the tooth fairy take her teeth. She wants to make jewelry out of them. She's perfectly weird and brave in all the best ways.
transcript.zh: 而且她还不让牙仙子把牙齿拿走，非要用自己的牙做成首饰。她在各种最美好的方面，既古灵精怪又勇敢无畏。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: So for her to shake and cry only with me is devastating. But also-- and I'm not proud of this-- a big part of me is like, girl, nobody's dying here. Suck it up.
transcript.zh: 所以一看到她只在我面前浑身发抖、哭个不停，我心都要碎了。但同时——说实话我并不以此为荣——我心里又有很大一部分在想：闺女，这又不是要命的事，忍一忍就过去了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Baby, I'm sorry. I have to get it.
transcript.zh: 宝贝，对不起，但这块我必须得梳开。

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: You already did.
transcript.zh: 你已经梳过了！

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I didn't.
transcript.zh: 还没有呢。

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Will it hurt always?
transcript.zh: 它以后一直都会这么疼吗？

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Probably, baby. Sometimes the things that we need are not comfortable.
transcript.zh: 大概吧，宝贝。有时候，我们真正需要的东西，就是没那么舒服。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Hold up. Did I just actually say that? I'm not even sure I believe it.
transcript.zh: 等一下，刚才那话真的是我说的吗？我自己都不确定信不信这一套。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: You know that moment when you open your mouth to say something and out comes your mother? This is one of the few times I heard that in my life, and it really stuck with me.
transcript.zh: 你懂那种感觉吧——刚一张嘴想说点什么，结果脱口而出的全是你妈的话？这辈子我就撞见过这么几回，而且那句话一直在我脑子里挥之不去。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Myra's mom was the Black female dean of a military college. Wait—My mom was the Black female dean of a military college. She taught me that sometimes in life, there are things like hair that you just have to tough out.
transcript.zh: 我妈曾是一所军事学院的黑人女性院长。她从小就教导我，人生在世，有些事——比如梳头——就是得咬牙硬扛过去。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: In so much of my parenting, I've tried to be a little different, do it my way. I don't know if I totally believe that Black kids should just have to tough it out when they're in pain.
transcript.zh: 在育儿这件事上，我大多数时候都想做点不一样的尝试，按自己的方式来。我不确定自己是否真的认同，黑人小孩在感到疼痛时就非得硬扛不可。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I also don't want to be a parent that teaches their Black kid that everything in life should feel like a lukewarm bath.
transcript.zh: 但与此同时，我也不想做一个把黑人孩子教成“生活里的一切都该像温水澡一样舒坦”的家长。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: When it comes to Avalon's hair, I feel so conflicted, like my two parenting styles are at war.
transcript.zh: 一碰到 Avalon 的头发，我整个人就特别撕裂，仿佛我体内的两种育儿观念在打架。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And when I heard myself say, sometimes the things we need are not comfortable, I felt like I had to talk to my mom about it. I needed her to back me up on this. So I called her.
transcript.zh: 当我听到自己说出“有时候我们需要的东西就是没那么舒服”时，我觉得必须跟老妈好好聊聊这事。我需要她给我撑腰，于是我给她打了个电话。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Miss Martha Mathis herself. I walked her through what had been going on with Avalon, the battle with her hair every day right before school.
transcript.zh: 也就是 Martha Mathis 女士本人。我把 Avalon 这阵子的情况跟她讲了一遍，说每天上学前为了梳头都要展开一番拉锯战。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And I asked her, this is just the way it is, right? To which she said—
transcript.zh: 我还问她，本来就是这样的，对吧？结果她说——

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: No, I think I've found that's what you want to avoid, because at some point, if you're rushing and you're trying to do our hair, then it's going to hurt.
transcript.zh: 不，我觉得这恰恰是要避免的，因为到了一定时候，如果你又赶时间又要打理咱们这种头发，那肯定会疼的。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: If it's going to sit up there for days without anybody doing anything, then you're going to get what you get.
transcript.zh: 要是放着好几天没人管，那最后打结成什么样就只能受着了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: My mom saying pain was something that you should or even could avoid was wild to me. She did my hair up so tightly I got migraines at school.
transcript.zh: 听我妈说这种疼是“应该”甚至“可以”避免的，我简直不敢相信。她以前帮我扎头发扯得太紧，害我在学校都犯偏头痛。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Mama, do you remember one time when you were doing my hair, and you were doing it and doing it, and I was like, ow, ow! And I was eating breakfast at the breakfast table, and then I threw up?
transcript.zh: 妈，你记不记得有一次你给我梳头，扯啊扯啊，我一直在那儿喊“好痛好痛”！当时我还在餐桌旁吃早饭，结果直接吐了出来？

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 不记得。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: You don't remember that?
transcript.zh: 你不记得这事了？

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: I don't, but that doesn't mean it didn't happen. It just means I don't remember it.
transcript.zh: 是不记得了，但这不代表没发生过，只是我没印象了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 嗯。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Then what did we do?
transcript.zh: 那后来我们怎么弄的？

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Oh, you went and grabbed the trash can, just in case I had to again. But yeah, I just remember it hurting a lot.
transcript.zh: 哦，你去把垃圾桶拎了过来，以防我待会儿还要吐。不过说真的，我就记得当时特别疼。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Oh, yeah.
transcript.zh: 哦，是啊。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: My mom once described my parenting style as permissive. Sometimes I feel like I have to be firmer when she's around, so she'll be proud of me, or something like that.
transcript.zh: 我妈以前形容我的育儿方式太纵容了。有时候她在旁边，我就觉得自己得严厉点，好让她觉得我做得不错，或者诸如此类的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: So I couldn't quite wrap my head around what I was hearing.
transcript.zh: 所以听到她这么说，我一时有点转不过弯来。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I'm kind of surprised to hear you say that, no, it doesn't have to hurt. I feel like you're a tough cookie, Mama.
transcript.zh: 听到你说“不，没必要弄得这么疼”，我其实挺惊讶的。妈，我觉得你一直是个很硬核的人。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: I am.
transcript.zh: 我是。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Yeah. And I feel like you kind of raised me to be one. And I can feel that lesson starting as early as my hair, right? Just as I can feel like I'm doing that with Avalon.
transcript.zh: 对啊。我觉得你也把我培养成了这样的人。而且我能感觉到这种教育从你给我梳头时就开始了，对吧？就像我现在能感觉到自己也在对 Avalon 这么做一样。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Do you think that I should be making her tough for the world? Like the way I'm talking about hair is kind of a gateway into, like, toughen up. Do you think that—
transcript.zh: 你觉得我应该磨炼她，让她坚强起来去面对这个世界吗？就像我把梳头当成一种“给我坚强点”的入门课。你觉得——

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: No. I wouldn't use hair as a gateway to toughen up because it has too many other racist and sexist implications.
transcript.zh: 不。我不会拿头发当成磨炼意志的途径，因为这背后牵扯了太多种族主义和性别歧视的意味。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Did you want me to toughen up in those moments when I was crying and like, ouch, this hurts?
transcript.zh: 那以前我一边哭一边喊“哎哟好疼”的时候，你难道不是想让我忍着点、坚强点吗？

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: No, no. It hurt. No. Why would you—no.
transcript.zh: 不是，不是。那是真疼啊。怎么会呢——不是的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: You didn't want me to toughen up and just be like, we got to get used to this because we're on a schedule, we got places to go?
transcript.zh: 你不是想让我坚强点，觉得“咱们得习惯，因为时间不等人，还得赶着出门”吗？

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Well, it was going to happen whether you were tough or not. And at six—I'll use Avalon's age—she's as tough as she's going to be right now. And she can't be any tougher.
transcript.zh: 哎呀，不管你坚不坚强，这头都得梳完。而且六岁——我就拿 Avalon 的年纪来说吧——她现在已经坚强到头了，不可能再比这更坚强了。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: I think she's the toughest little girl I know. So no, I would not have equated doing your hair with tough or not. I always felt bad that for those 10, 15, how many ever minutes it was, that that's how you were starting your day.
transcript.zh: 她已经是我见过最坚强的小姑娘了。所以不会，我绝不会把梳头跟坚不坚强画等号。每次想到那十来十五分钟——不管当时花了多久——你每天的一早都要这么开头，我心里其实一直很过意不去。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I didn't know that she'd had any feelings about our mornings. My mother told me it was the same for her when she was young.
transcript.zh: 我完全不知道她对我们当年每天早上的梳头还有过这些感受。我妈告诉我，她小时候也是一模一样的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: She sat between her mother's knees, and out came the hot combs, the hair grease, the brushes, the pain, which she likes to remind me was far worse than mine, as I remind my daughter, and we copy and paste.
transcript.zh: 她坐在我外婆两膝之间，热烫梳、发油、硬毛刷还有疼痛轮番上阵——她总喜欢提醒我她那会儿受的罪比我惨多了，就像我也会这样提醒我女儿，于是我们把这套模式原封不动地复制粘贴了下来。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: But instead of giving me the validation I wanted and letting me know that the way she'd done my hair is really the only way, my mom gave me some advice I really wasn't looking for.
transcript.zh: 但我本想从她那儿得到认同，想听她说当年她给我梳头的方式确实是唯一办法，结果我妈却给了我一个我压根没想到的建议。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Give her some of her own hair.
transcript.zh: 分一部分头发让她自己管。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Oh, to take care of? Yes, I've tried this. We've tried this, yes.
transcript.zh: 哦，让她自己打理吗？嗯，我试过，我们试过的。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Oh, you have?
transcript.zh: 哦，你们试过啦？

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Oh, yeah. We've tried—it's do-your-own-hair day.
transcript.zh: 对啊，我们搞过什么“自己梳头日”。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Do-your-own-hair day in my house means we give Avalon a brush and some bows, and 15 minutes later, absolutely nothing has happened. But it turned out that wasn't what my mother was suggesting.
transcript.zh: 在我们家，所谓“自己梳头日”，就是给 Avalon 一把梳子和几个蝴蝶结，结果十五分钟过去，头发一根都没动。不过后来我才明白，我妈说的并不是这个意思。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: No, I mean, have her do her own kitchen.
transcript.zh: 不，我是说，让她自己弄后颈发际线那块碎发。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Well.
transcript.zh: 这个嘛……

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: She'll be gentle with herself.
transcript.zh: 她对自己下手肯定会轻一点。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: If she does her own hair at this age, Mama, she's avoiding her kitchen altogether.
transcript.zh: 妈，她这么点大要是自己梳头，肯定直接绕开后颈那块不管了。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Okay. So it looks like, I don't know, a rat's nest. Nobody's going to see it.
transcript.zh: 行啊，就算乱得像个鸡窝又怎样？反正后脑勺下面别人也看不见。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 也是。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: And if you remind her, now get in there, because you don't want me in there. When you remind her of that, it's going to be your hand or mine.
transcript.zh: 而且你可以提醒她：“自己伸手去把那儿理顺了，不然就得妈妈动手咯。”你这么一提醒，她就知道要么自己动手，要么挨你的手。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 嗯。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: I think if you give her something that she owns, and if it's just this little bit back there, my goodness, let her have it. What would happen if you parted that off, though, seriously?
transcript.zh: 我觉得，哪怕只是后脑勺下面那么一小撮，只要分给她让她自己做主，天哪，就随她去吧。说真的，你要是真把那一块分出来归她管，能出什么大事呢？

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I'm hearing you. I just don't—I'm like, when you're saying, why don't you try this, why don't you try giving Avalon a little section for herself, why didn't you try that with me?
transcript.zh: 我听明白了。只是我忍不住想——听你现在说“怎么不试试分一小撮头发给 Avalon 自己弄”，那当年你怎么没对我试过这招呢？

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: Because no one told me that. That's how—
transcript.zh: 因为当年没人教过我这些呀。这些观念就是这样——

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: messages are passed on. The women my age, they were not brought up to even have these kind of conversations. And I don't even know if I had them in my brain, I mean, back then.
transcript.zh: 代代相传的。我这个年纪的女人，从小根本没人教过我们去聊这种事。甚至当年我脑子里压根就没想过这些。

transcript.speaker: Martha Mathis
transcript.en: But I'm saying for you, I would think you do have options. When you know better, you do better.
transcript.zh: 但我的意思是，放到你这代，我觉得你是有的选的。懂得多了，自然就能做得更好。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: The next time I did Avalon's hair, I let her do some of it.
transcript.zh: 下次再给 Avalon 梳头时，我让她自己动手弄了一小块。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: You ready to get the back, just a little bit right here? Good job. Back here.
transcript.zh: 准备好自己梳后面这儿了吗，就这儿一点点？真棒，就这后面。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Look at that! Why are you smiling? Whenever Mama's doing it, you're crying.
transcript.zh: 瞧你这样！怎么还笑起来了？每次妈妈给你梳头的时候，你可都是哭唧唧的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: What's it feel like to do your own hair?
transcript.zh: 自己给自己梳头是什么感觉呀？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Soft.
transcript.zh: 软软的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: It feels soft, huh?
transcript.zh: 感觉软软的，是吗？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: It doesn't feel hard like a rock. But when Mama does it, it feels hard like a rock.
transcript.zh: 摸起来不像石头那么硬。可是妈妈给我梳的时候，就像石头一样硬邦邦的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Your hair feels hard like a rock, or my brushing feels hard like a rock?
transcript.zh: 是你的头发像石头一样硬，还是妈妈梳得太重像石头一样硬？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: The brushing feels hard like a rock.
transcript.zh: 是梳得像石头一样硬。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Does this part hurt?
transcript.zh: 这块儿疼不疼？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 不疼。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Oh, good. I don't think I've ever seen your kitchen look so good. Should we show Papa?
transcript.zh: 太好了。我觉得妈妈从来没见过你后颈这块儿的头发梳得这么好。要不要给爸爸看看？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Mm-hmm.
transcript.zh: 嗯！

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: Papa Bear! Do you want to tell him? Want to tell him?
transcript.zh: 熊爸爸！你要跟他说吗？想不想告诉他？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Look at my kitchen.
transcript.zh: 看我后颈这块儿的头发。

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.en: Wow.
transcript.zh: 哇哦。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: What about your kitchen?
transcript.zh: 你后颈这块儿怎么啦？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: I did it.
transcript.zh: 我自己弄的。

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.en: You did it?
transcript.zh: 你自己弄的呀？

transcript.speaker: Avalon
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 对呀。

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.en: Good job, baby.
transcript.zh: 真棒，宝贝。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: As a parent, you're always looking for your failures. There are so many ways to fall short.
transcript.zh: 为人父母，总是忍不住去盯自己做得不够好的地方。毕竟能掉链子的地方实在太多了。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: But every once in a while, if you're lucky, the evidence is clear. You did something really good for your kid.
transcript.zh: 但偶尔也有那么几次，如果运气好的话，成果会明明白白摆在眼前——你真真切切为孩子做了一件好事。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: And with my mom's help, I was able to change this one thing in the wheel of my own motherhood, and maybe one day, Avalon's.
transcript.zh: 在妈妈的帮助下，我终于扭转了自己身为母亲的人生轮回里的这一环，也许将来有一天，也能改变 Avalon 的。

transcript.speaker: Myra Flynn
transcript.en: I want her to know what my mother knew, and her mother before her, that when you're doing your hair, some parts need someone else's hands, and some parts we can learn to hold ourselves.
transcript.zh: 我希望她明白我母亲明白的道理，也是外婆当年教给母亲的道理：打理头发这件事，有些部分需要别人搭把手，而有些部分，我们得学会自己去握在手里。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Myra Flynn. She's the host of the podcast Homegoings with Myra Flynn, which is available wherever you get your podcasts. Her story was produced by Emmanuel Dzotsi.
transcript.zh: 以上故事来自 Myra Flynn。她是播客《Homegoings with Myra Flynn》的主持人，各大播客平台均可收听。她的这期故事由 Emmanuel Dzotsi 制作。
